questions.question: A property manager is creating a tenant 'satisfaction survey'. Which factor is MOST important when designing this survey?
answers: Ensuring that the survey is biased towards positive feedback to boost morale.
Ensuring that the survey is very long, to fully assess all areas of the tenant's experience.
Ensuring the survey is clear, concise, and encourages tenants to provide honest and actionable feedback.
Ensuring the survey is only provided to tenants that are considered reliable and happy.
feedbacks: This will not be an effective survey.
A lengthy survey will reduce participation.
This is the key factor for any survey.
This will bias the results.
questions.explanation: The main focus of a tenant satisfaction survey, is to ensure that tenants feel comfortable providing honest feedback, which can then be used to improve service.

questions.question: What is the significance of a 'certificate of occupancy' (CO) in property management?
answers: It confirms the ownership of the building and any associated land.
It outlines all the terms and conditions of a tenancy agreement for a particular property.
It verifies that the building complies with all local codes and can be legally occupied.
It confirms that all insurance premiums have been paid in full.
feedbacks: This is not a CO but a deed of ownership.
This is the function of a lease agreement.
This is the purpose of a CO.
This is not the purpose of a CO.
questions.explanation: A CO is issued by a local authority when a building has been built in line with all required codes and regulations. It allows the building to be legally occupied.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the function of a 'property maintenance log'?
answers: To keep track of tenant contact information and private data.
To provide a detailed record of all maintenance tasks, inspections, and repairs carried out at the property.
To only track the payments made to any maintenance vendors.
To act as a formal method of communication between tenants and maintenance staff.
feedbacks: This would be a tenant log not a maintenance log.
This is the core purpose of a maintenance log.
While important, this is not the only function of the log.
This is not the primary purpose of the log.
questions.explanation: A maintenance log should record all aspects of property maintenance and repairs.

questions.question: A property manager is evaluating bids for a new insurance policy. Which of the following is MOST important to consider when choosing a provider?
answers: The aesthetic design of the provider’s promotional materials.
The personal relationship between the property manager and the sales agent.
The coverage limits, deductibles, and any exclusions within the policy, and the reputation of the insurance provider.
The cheapest option available, regardless of the coverage provided.
feedbacks: This is not a key factor when choosing a provider.
A personal relationship is not a business consideration.
This is the key factor when assessing insurance.
Price should not be the main driver when assessing insurance cover.
questions.explanation: When assessing insurance cover, a manager must review all aspects of the policy and also the reputation and financial security of the insurance provider.

questions.question: A property manager has received a tenant request to 'sublet' their unit. What should be the FIRST step to take in addressing this?
answers: Ignore the request, as the tenant is legally bound to the terms of their original lease.
Immediately grant the request, as long as the rent continues to be paid in full.
Review the terms of the current lease to establish if subletting is permitted, and then discuss all options with the tenant.
Immediately refuse the request, as subletting is not allowed under any circumstances.
feedbacks: Ignoring the request will not resolve the issue.
The lease must be reviewed before any action is taken.
This is the best first step.
Subletting may be a permitted practice in the current lease.
questions.explanation: The lease must be reviewed to assess if subletting is permitted. Once reviewed, any potential action must be discussed and agreed with the tenant.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a property manager's responsibility in relation to 'Fair Housing Laws'?
answers: To always prioritize the property owner’s preferences over all other considerations.
To make sure all potential tenants are treated equally, without any discrimination based on protected characteristics.
To only focus on the properties that are in the best areas of the town or city.
To only focus on renting the property to groups that align with the owners personal views.
feedbacks: This will not comply with Fair Housing laws.
This is a key requirement of Fair Housing Laws.
This is not a requirement of Fair Housing laws.
This would be discriminatory and illegal.
questions.explanation: Fair Housing laws require that all tenants and applicants are treated equally and no one is discriminated against on the basis of their race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, or disability.

questions.question: A property manager needs to improve the overall 'tenant retention' rate for the property. Which action would be the most effective first step?
answers: To implement aggressive rent increases at the end of each lease agreement.
To ignore any tenant concerns to maintain a more efficient business.
To conduct a survey to gather feedback from tenants about areas for improvement.
To focus on marketing and attracting new tenants and ignoring any existing ones.
feedbacks: This would not improve tenant retention.
Ignoring tenants is bad practice and will reduce retention.
This is the correct first action.
This will not solve the problem of a low retention rate.
questions.explanation: Gathering feedback from tenants will provide the best insight into any issues with retention. This can be acted upon to improve the tenant experience.

questions.question: What is the significance of a 'holdover' clause in a lease agreement?
answers: It allows the landlord to increase the rent during the term of a fixed lease.
It allows a tenant to break their lease early without any financial penalties.
It sets the terms for the continuation of a lease after it has officially expired.
It sets the conditions for a lease to be extended beyond the expiry date with changes to the terms of the agreement.
feedbacks: This is not the purpose of the holdover clause.
This is not what the holdover clause is used for.
This is the meaning of the holdover clause.
This is not the purpose of the holdover clause.
questions.explanation: A holdover clause sets the terms of a lease when a tenant remains in place after the lease has expired. This will usually convert the lease to a month-to-month arrangement.

questions.question: A property manager is reviewing the 'capital expenditures' for a property. Which of the following is a good example of capex?
answers: The monthly payments for general cleaning services.
The routine replacement of lightbulbs in the communal areas.
The cost of installing a new roof on the property.
The cost of electricity used to power the lighting in the property.
feedbacks: This is part of opex not capex.
This is a routine repair and a part of opex.
This is an example of a capital expenditure.
This is part of the operational expenses not capital.
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure is money spent on projects that improve, or extend the life of the building.

questions.question: A property manager is developing a 'disaster preparedness plan' for a multi-unit building. Which of the following is most important for its success?
answers: To only focus on the financial aspects of any potential disaster and its recovery.
To focus solely on the building structure and neglect any consideration for tenants.
To ensure there is a clear, well communicated strategy for all tenants, staff and any other key parties to follow.
To only include the property manager as a key contact for any emergencies.
feedbacks: Financials are only part of a disaster plan.
The tenant's wellbeing is a priority.
This is the main element of a successful disaster plan.
It is important to have more than one point of contact.
questions.explanation: A disaster plan must be clear, well communicated to all parties, and have clear steps for all to follow in the event of an emergency.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the goal of a ‘property maintenance schedule’ for a rental property?
answers: To delay all maintenance tasks for as long as possible to reduce overall costs.
To make sure only repairs are carried out when there is an immediate emergency.
To proactively schedule regular inspections and preventative maintenance, to minimize the potential for larger issues in the future.
To ensure that all tenants are aware of all repairs and maintenance that has taken place.
feedbacks: This will likely increase the costs in the future.
This is not effective property maintenance.
This is the correct aim of a maintenance schedule.
This is part of the communication process not the maintenance schedule.
questions.explanation: A maintenance schedule plans the maintenance of a property to ensure the quality and safety is maintained. The aim is to prevent large issues from occurring through regular maintenance.

questions.question: A property manager is required to handle tenant complaints effectively. What should they prioritize when managing this process?
answers: To always side with the tenant with the longest standing tenancy.
To always prioritize the landlords view, as they are the property owner.
To always act with impartiality, and be transparent in all dealings whilst seeking a resolution that is fair for all parties.
To ignore all complaints and hope they will resolve themselves in time.
feedbacks: This is not an effective strategy for handling complaints.
This would not be a fair or impartial method of resolution.
This is the correct way to resolve complaints.
Ignoring complaints will cause escalation.
questions.explanation: Effective complaint management requires an impartial approach, transparency, and a fair solution for all parties involved.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a 'lease audit' in property management?
answers: To determine if rent increases are required at the end of each lease.
To review all tenant payment records and confirm there are no late payments.
To confirm the accuracy of the terms and conditions of all existing leases and assess compliance with lease agreements.
To find any lease clauses that could be disputed or removed.
feedbacks: This is not the key purpose of a lease audit.
This would form part of a financial audit and not the lease audit.
This is the main focus of a lease audit.
This is not the aim of a lease audit.
questions.explanation: The aim of a lease audit is to review all terms and conditions of existing leases, to confirm compliance with all agreements.

questions.question: A property manager needs to make some large scale 'capital improvements' to a property. Which of the following best describes the purpose of these improvements?
answers: To ensure minor repairs are completed in an efficient and timely manner.
To ensure the property looks aesthetically pleasing to attract more prospective tenants.
To increase the long term value, lifespan and the efficiency of the property.
To reduce short term costs by ignoring or delaying any required maintenance.
feedbacks: These are routine maintenance tasks not capex.
While important, this is not the main purpose of capex.
This is the key aim of capital improvements.
This would have a negative impact on the long term value.
questions.explanation: Capital improvements are undertaken to increase the long term value, lifespan, and efficiency of a building, therefore increasing the overall asset value.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes a property manager's responsibility when it comes to tenant 'privacy'?
answers: To only focus on protecting tenant data if they specifically ask to be protected.
To ensure all personal information, is kept safe and secure, and only shared when required for the purpose of running the property.
To freely share any personal tenant data with any interested third parties.
To ignore all data protection laws if it is deemed that it is not of relevance to the tenants.
feedbacks: The data must be protected irrespective of a specific request.
This is a key responsibility of the property manager.
This would be a violation of tenant privacy laws.
This is a violation of privacy laws.
questions.explanation: Tenant privacy is a legal requirement. A property manager must protect all data from unapproved access, and only share when there is a valid business need.

questions.question: A property manager is conducting a 'risk assessment' for a managed property. Which of the following is a key area that must be assessed?
answers: Any potential safety hazards or environmental risks on the property.
The total annual revenue of the property, and its profitability.
Any historical maintenance records and past incidents that may highlight issues.
Any potential breaches of privacy or data protection laws.
Any potential for increases in local rent rates in the coming months.
The overall curb appeal of the building and its external appearance.
feedbacks: This is required for risk assessment.
This is not part of a risk assessment.
This is a key element for assessing risk.
Data security is part of the risk assessment process.
This is part of a market assessment not the risk assessment.
This is not part of the risk assessment process.
questions.explanation: Safety issues, historical incidents, and data security all form part of a comprehensive risk assessment plan.

questions.question: What is the definition of 'Net Cash Flow' in property management?
answers: The effective gross income minus all property operating expenses.
The gross potential rental income minus all associated costs.
The net operating income minus all debt service payments.
The total amount of rent collected minus any capital expenditure costs.
feedbacks: This is the formula for net operating income not cash flow.
This is not the net cash flow.
This is the correct formula for net cash flow.
This is not the net cash flow, and only takes into account capex.
questions.explanation: Net cash flow is the result of deducting all debt servicing costs from the Net Operating Income.

questions.question: A property manager is developing a new 'tenant portal'. What should be a primary focus during the design and implementation?
answers: To only focus on the needs of the property manager and not the tenants.
To ensure the portal is complex and difficult to use to prevent tenants from requesting unnecessary data.
To ensure the portal is simple, easy to use, accessible, secure, and offers a wide range of useful information for all tenants.
To ensure that all data on the portal is kept private from the tenants.
feedbacks: This would be an ineffective design process.
This is not an effective way to provide information to tenants.
This is the best approach when creating a new portal.
The portal must be useful for tenants and should provide the data they require.
questions.explanation: The portal must be designed for ease of use by tenants, whilst offering all required functionality. Security, and privacy of data must be at the forefront of the design process.

questions.question: A property manager is responsible for the ethical management of a property. What does this require them to do?
answers: To prioritize profits at all costs, even if it harms tenants or the local community.
To always act with complete transparency, integrity, and fairness in all dealings, while also protecting the interests of the property owner.
To focus on only the short term goals and profit of the property, regardless of long term impacts.
To only focus on implementing rules and regulations that are beneficial to the property owner.
feedbacks: This would not be ethical behavior.
This is the main requirement of ethical behavior.
This is not an ethical way to manage property.
This would be unethical and bias towards the owner.
questions.explanation: Ethical management requires transparency, integrity, fairness to all parties, whilst also protecting the interests of the property owner.

questions.question: A property manager has received a complaint about a potential 'environmental issue' on the property. What should be the first action taken?
answers: To immediately contact a contractor to resolve the issue, without a proper assessment.
To ignore the issue and hope it will resolve itself over time.
To conduct a full assessment of the issue to identify the nature and scope of the problem before taking any action.
To immediately report the issue to the local environmental health authority.
feedbacks: This could be wasteful and not identify the true source of the problem.
This is not an acceptable course of action when there is a potential environmental hazard.
This is the correct first step.
The manager should carry out their own assessment before escalating the problem.
questions.explanation: A full assessment is required before any action, this must identify the issue and also the potential cause and scope of the problem.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a 'property management agreement'?
answers: To define the terms of a lease agreement between a landlord and a tenant.
To set out the duties, responsibilities and scope of work between a property manager and the owner of the property.
To confirm the accuracy of all financial transactions in a given financial year.
To detail any disputes between the tenants living at a property.
feedbacks: This is the function of a lease agreement, not a management agreement.
This is the correct definition of a property management agreement.
This is part of an audit process not the management agreement.
This is not the purpose of a management agreement.
questions.explanation: A property management agreement outlines all responsibilities, duties, and expectations of both the property owner and the property manager.

questions.question: A property manager needs to ensure the 'safety of tenants'. Which action should be their highest priority?
answers: To only focus on minor aesthetic repairs rather than more serious safety issues.
To only make safety repairs when specifically requested by a tenant.
To make sure all safety regulations are met, and to proactively reduce any potential hazards, through regular inspections and maintenance.
To minimize any costs associated with safety by ignoring any minor safety concerns.
feedbacks: This will have a negative impact on safety.
Safety repairs should be made irrespective of tenant requests.
This is the key responsibility of the manager.
This is not an acceptable practice.
questions.explanation: Tenant safety is paramount, all aspects of the property must be safe, hazards must be identified and resolved, and all required safety regulations must be followed.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a property manager's responsibility regarding 'tenant screening'?
answers: To only screen tenants that the property manager considers to be a good fit for the property.
To ensure all tenants are screened in a consistent manner, using a fair and impartial process, whilst also adhering to all relevant laws and legislation.
To ignore all tenant screening as long as they are able to pay the rent each month.
To discriminate against any applicant that is not from a particular background.
feedbacks: This is bias and not the correct approach.
This is the correct approach for tenant screening.
This is not good practice and may create issues in the long term.
This is not compliant and illegal.
questions.explanation: Tenant screening must be fair, consistent, impartial, and must not discriminate against any protected characteristics. It must also comply with all local laws.

questions.question: What does the term 'amortization' refer to in property management accounting?
answers: The cost of all new capital expenditure projects on the property.
The process of allocating the cost of an intangible asset over a set period of time.
The interest rate that is charged on any debts for the property.
The estimated loss of value of a property due to wear and tear.
feedbacks: This would be part of capex not amortization.
This is the purpose of amortization.
This is a finance cost not amortization.
This would be depreciation.
questions.explanation: Amortization is an accounting process that spreads the cost of an intangible asset over a predetermined life span.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary factor in a 'market analysis' for a rental property?
answers: The number of tenants that are currently living in the property.
The location of the property and the surrounding amenities.
The current average rental rates in the local area.
The financial history of previous tenants that have lived in the property.
The demand for rental properties, and any vacancy rates in the local market.
The personal preferences of the property manager in regards to rental rates.
feedbacks: This is not a part of a market analysis.
This is a required element of market analysis.
This is a key part of market analysis.
This is not relevant in a market analysis.
This is key to market analysis.
This is not a factor in the analysis.
questions.explanation: Location, current rental rates, and the demand for rental properties are all key areas of a good market analysis.

questions.question: A property manager is tasked with creating a 'pro forma' for a potential property purchase. What should be the MAIN focus of this document?
answers: To detail all tenant complaints from the previous tenancy.
To provide an assessment of the overall current condition of the property.
To provide a detailed assessment of the potential income, costs and profitability of the property.
To act as a legal document that defines the terms of sale.
feedbacks: This is not relevant to a pro forma.
This is part of the due diligence process not the pro forma.
This is the main purpose of the pro forma document.
This is the function of the sales contract not the pro forma.
questions.explanation: The pro forma is a financial tool that provides a forecast of the potential costs, income and profits of a prospective property purchase.

questions.question: What is the definition of 'Effective Gross Income' (EGI) in property management?
answers: The total amount of revenue collected from all tenants.
The maximum amount of rent that could be collected if all units were occupied.
The gross potential rental income minus any vacancy and credit losses.
The total rental revenue of a property minus all of the operating expenses.
feedbacks: This does not take into account any vacancies.
This would be the gross potential income.
This is the correct definition of effective gross income.
This would be the net operating income not the effective gross income.
questions.explanation: Effective gross income is calculated by subtracting vacancy and credit losses from the potential gross income of the property.

questions.question: A property manager is reviewing their existing 'lease agreements'. Which aspect is most important to ensure they are fit for purpose?
answers: That all leases are identical, to make them easier to manage.
That all lease terms and conditions are in compliance with all local and federal laws and legislation.
That all the lease terms are in line with the personal views of the property manager.
That they provide maximum profit for the property owner regardless of tenant requirements.
feedbacks: All leases need to be tailored to the property and the needs of the tenants.
This is the most important factor.
Personal preference is not a key driver in any legal document.
This is not the main requirement of a lease.
questions.explanation: A lease must be compliant with all laws and legislation, it must clearly define all terms and conditions and should be fair and balanced for all parties.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an 'SNDA' (Subordination, Non-Disturbance, and Attornment) clause in a lease agreement?
answers: To set the terms for a quick and simple eviction of the tenant.
To set the terms for a tenant to sublet the property to any party without permission from the owner.
To protect the rights of the tenant in the event of the property being sold or foreclosed upon.
To provide a method of rent reduction in the event of a change in circumstances.
feedbacks: This is not the purpose of the SNDA clause.
Subletting is separate from the SNDA clause.
This is the purpose of the SNDA clause.
This is not the role of the SNDA clause.
questions.explanation: The SNDA clause is used to ensure the tenant’s rights are protected if the property changes hands or there is a foreclosure.

questions.question: A property manager has a responsibility to provide 'reasonable accommodation' to tenants with disabilities. Which of the following best describes this responsibility?
answers: To ignore all requests to avoid the risk of any further complications on the property.
To provide any modification at the tenant's request, regardless of the cost or impact on the property.
To provide reasonable changes or modifications to a property that are required to accommodate a tenant, as long as there is no undue hardship to the landlord.
To only offer accommodation to tenants that do not require any special accommodations or alterations to the property.
feedbacks: This is illegal and non compliant.
This is not a reasonable approach to this issue.
This is the correct definition of reasonable accommodation.
This is discriminatory and illegal.
questions.explanation: Reasonable accommodation requires a property manager to meet any reasonable request for modifications or alterations to a property, unless it would create an undue hardship for the owner.

questions.question: A property manager is developing a 'preventative maintenance' schedule for a property. Which aspect should be prioritized?
answers: To only complete the minimum possible tasks to ensure a reduction in running costs.
To only perform maintenance when requested by tenants, to reduce unnecessary work.
To schedule regular inspections and maintenance tasks based on the needs and specific aspects of the property.
To only focus on the areas of the property that the property manager considers to be important.
feedbacks: This approach will cause issues in the long term.
This will not stop future maintenance problems.
This is the best method when creating a schedule.
This is not the correct approach for maintenance.
questions.explanation: Preventative maintenance schedules should be driven by the specific needs and requirements of the property, whilst also making sure to resolve all known issues.

questions.question: A property manager has a responsibility to maintain 'accurate financial records'. Which of the following actions best ensures that they do this?
answers: To keep all financial records in a private account and only share them when the owner requests them.
To make sure all records are accurate, complete and available for review when required, whilst also storing them in a safe and secure location.
To use a cash based system of accounting to make it easier to track payments.
To only focus on the major financial transactions, and not keep records of smaller or minor outgoings.
feedbacks: This is not transparent and poor practice.
This is the best practice when keeping financial records.
This is not a generally accepted accounting practice.
This is not accurate and could lead to problems.
questions.explanation: Good financial record keeping requires accuracy, transparency, and all records to be available for review. They must also be securely stored to prevent loss.

questions.question: A property manager is reviewing bids for a new 'property management software' system. What factor is MOST important when making a selection?
answers: That the software is simple to use, effective, provides a range of useful functionality and is compatible with all existing hardware and software.
That the software is the cheapest option possible, to keep costs down.
That the software is the most attractive, with the best user interface.
That the software is only able to be used by the property manager and no other staff.
feedbacks: This is the correct way to select the best software.
Cost should not be the only driver when selecting software.
This is not a good metric for business software selection.
The software should be available for all staff.
questions.explanation: The most important factor when choosing software is its usability, compatibility, efficiency and the functionality it provides.

questions.question: A property manager is trying to maximize the 'energy efficiency' of a property. Which of the following is the LEAST effective way to achieve this?
answers: Installing new energy efficient windows that prevent heat loss.
Using highly inefficient single use lighting with no energy saving properties.
Implementing a program of regular maintenance for all HVAC systems.
Installing renewable energy sources to generate clean energy.
feedbacks: This would be a good way to improve efficiency.
This will not improve energy efficiency.
This will help to maintain efficiency.
This will reduce energy consumption from the grid.
questions.explanation: Using energy inefficient lighting will negatively impact the efficiency of the property, and lead to higher energy bills.

questions.question: What is the definition of 'Net Operating Income' (NOI) in property management?
answers: The total annual revenue collected by a property.
The gross rental revenue minus any vacancy rates and credit losses.
The effective gross income minus the total operating expenses of the property.
The total operating costs of the property minus all rental revenue.
feedbacks: This is the gross revenue not the NOI.
This is the effective gross income, not the NOI.
This is the correct definition of net operating income.
This is not NOI, it would be a net loss.
questions.explanation: NOI is a calculation of the revenue of a building minus all of its operating costs. It is the number used before any debt servicing costs are deducted.

questions.question: A property manager has a legal responsibility to provide 'safe and habitable' conditions for all tenants. What does this entail?
answers: Ensuring that the property is as cheap to maintain as possible regardless of safety.
Ensuring that the property is free from hazards, and meets all relevant legal codes and regulations.
Ensuring that only minor repairs are completed to keep running costs to a minimum.
Only completing safety repairs when they are specifically requested by a tenant.
feedbacks: This would be unacceptable and would not meet the obligations.
This is the best description of a property manager's responsibility.
This would not meet the requirement for safety and habitability.
Repairs are required to meet obligations irrespective of tenant requests.
questions.explanation: A property must be free from hazards, and comply with all codes and regulations, in order to be safe and habitable for its tenants.

questions.question: A property manager is developing a 'tenant communication plan'. What aspect should be the PRIMARY focus?
answers: To create a plan that will only benefit the property manager, and not the tenant.
To use a complicated and confusing method to ensure fewer tenants contact them directly.
To create a plan that is clear, timely, and accessible to all tenants, offering multiple channels of communication.
To use only one method of communication to make it easier for the property manager to manage.
feedbacks: A communication plan must benefit all parties.
This is not a good approach to tenant communication.
This is the main focus of the plan.
Using multiple methods is required.
questions.explanation: An effective communication plan must be timely, clear and accessible to all. It must also provide a range of communication channels to suit all tenants.

questions.question: A property manager is tasked with creating a 'risk management plan' for a property. Which action is MOST important during this process?
answers: To ignore all historical records and start the process with a blank template.
To identify all potential risks, and then develop clear plans for how to minimize these risks and resolve them quickly and efficiently.
To only focus on the financial risks, and ignore the safety risks on the property.
To only plan for risks that have previously occurred on the property.
feedbacks: Historical records can be very useful.
This is the correct approach when creating a risk management plan.
All areas of risk must be assessed.
The plan must assess all potential risks not just historical ones.
questions.explanation: Risk management is a systematic process that identifies potential hazards and then creates a plan to minimize the risk and resolve issues quickly.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a 'lease option' agreement in real estate?
answers: To reduce the amount of monthly rent for a tenant.
To provide the tenant the option to purchase the property at a predetermined price, during the time period of the lease.
To allow the tenant to sublet the property without the knowledge of the owner.
To allow the landlord to increase the rent on a property during the term of a lease agreement.
feedbacks: This is not the function of a lease option.
This is the purpose of the lease option.
This is not the function of a lease option agreement.
This is not the function of the lease option.
questions.explanation: A lease option agreement provides a tenant with the option to buy a property during a set period, at a pre-agreed price.

questions.question: A property manager is developing a 'marketing strategy' for a vacant property. Which aspect should be the main focus?
answers: To try and attract the largest possible number of potential applicants, regardless of their suitability.
To try and overstate the qualities of the property, whilst ignoring or hiding any negative aspects.
To target suitable prospective tenants and highlight the property’s key features, and benefits that will match their specific needs.
To set the rental rates as high as possible, regardless of the current market conditions.
feedbacks: Attracting unsuitable tenants is not effective.
This is an unethical and ineffective approach.
This is the correct strategy for effective marketing.
This would be ineffective and likely lead to vacancies.
questions.explanation: Marketing should focus on the key qualities of a property, targeting the right tenants, whilst also ensuring that the rental rates are in line with the current local market.

questions.question: A property manager is required to keep 'accurate records' of all property related finances. Which of the following is the MOST important step in doing this?
answers: To keep all accounting records as private as possible, and only share them with the owner.
To make sure all financial transactions are correctly recorded, with full documentation, and that all records are securely stored, and easily retrievable.
To use a simple cash based accounting method to ensure that all records are easy to manage.
To only record any large amounts of money, and ignore any smaller or minor transactions.
feedbacks: This would be poor practice and is not transparent.
This is the key factor in accurate financial record keeping.
This is not a generally accepted method of accounting.
All transactions need to be recorded for accuracy.
questions.explanation: Accurate record keeping must include full documentation, accurate records of all transactions, and the records must be securely stored and easily accessible.

questions.question: A property manager is responsible for handling a 'tenant emergency'. Which action should be taken FIRST?
answers: To protect the property from any further damage.
To try and reduce the overall costs of the resolution.
To ensure the tenant is safe and has everything they need, then assess any property damage.
To contact the insurance company immediately to make a claim.
feedbacks: The safety of the tenant must be prioritized over property damage.
Costs should not be considered when dealing with an emergency.
This is the most important first step.
This can wait until after the tenant has been made safe.
questions.explanation: The safety of the tenant is the key element of any emergency, this must be made the priority at all times.

questions.question: A property manager is conducting a 'lease audit'. What is the PRIMARY focus of this audit?
answers: To review all historical financial records from past tenancies.
To assess if the current rental rates are in line with the market and should be increased.
To determine if all lease terms are in compliance with the agreement, and that all relevant policies have been adhered to.
To review if the property is meeting all current local building regulations and codes.
feedbacks: This is part of a financial audit not a lease audit.
This is done as part of market analysis not a lease audit.
This is the purpose of a lease audit.

questions.question: A property manager is working to increase the 'energy efficiency' of a property. Which of the following is the MOST effective approach?

questions.question: Which of the following is a key responsibility for a property manager when handling 'tenant complaints'?

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the primary focus of a ‘property marketing plan’ for a vacant commercial space?

questions.question: A property manager is tasked with handling a 'tenant eviction'. Which action should be prioritized during this process?
answers: To try and complete the eviction as quickly and efficiently as possible, without any regard for legal procedures.

questions.question: A property manager is reviewing a new insurance policy. What is the MOST important aspect to assess before taking out a policy?

The price of the premium, regardless of the level of cover that it provides.

questions.question: What is the definition of 'depreciation' in accounting terms, as it relates to a building?

The allocation of the purchase cost of a building over its useful lifespan.

questions.question: A property manager has a responsibility to act ethically. Which of the following best describes this requirement?
answers: To always prioritize the needs of the property owner over all other factors.

questions.question: A property manager is creating a new 'tenant communication plan'. What is the main focus for any plan?

answers: Only focusing on historical risks from the property and ignoring any potential new ones.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of a 'preventative maintenance' program for a managed property?
answers: To only respond to maintenance emergencies that are reported by tenants.
To reduce the cost of maintenance by delaying all work until it is critical and cannot be avoided.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST important for a property manager to consider when selecting a new 'tenant screening service'?

questions.question: A property manager has a legal obligation to comply with all local 'zoning laws'. What does this entail?

feedbacks: This is the opposite of what the warranty implies.
This is the main aspect of the warranty of habitability.
This is not correct, the landlord does have a legal responsibility for the upkeep of a property.
This is a breach of the quiet enjoyment clause.
questions.explanation: Warranty of habitability means that the landlord is legally responsible for providing a safe and habitable property for its tenants.

questions.question: A property manager is implementing a new ‘tenant portal’. Which of the following is MOST important to consider during the planning stages?
answers: That the system is only designed to benefit the property management team, and that the needs of the tenants are not a key factor.
That the system is as complex as possible, and that tenants will need a degree of training to be able to use it effectively.
That the system is intuitive, easy to use, secure, and that it meets the needs of both the tenants and also the property management team.
That the system is only accessible by the property manager, and that no other staff member is authorized to have access.
feedbacks: This is not an effective way to create a system.
Complex systems are hard to adopt and may be detrimental to take up.
This is the most effective approach when implementing new software.
This may not be practical in a larger business.
questions.explanation: New systems should be designed for easy use and must provide value for all parties. The system should be fully functional, secure and accessible to those that need access.

questions.question: A property manager is required to comply with all ‘local zoning laws’. Which of the following is an example of how they must meet this requirement?
answers: To only comply with zoning laws if the property owner requests that they do so.
To ignore all zoning laws as long as they do not create any major impact on the local area.
To ensure that all properties are used in accordance with their correct zoning classification and that they comply with all associated regulations.
To only comply with zoning laws if the building is being used as a residential unit, and not a commercial property.
feedbacks: Compliance is mandatory.
This is illegal and does not meet requirements.
This is the key purpose of zoning compliance.
Zoning laws apply to all properties.
questions.explanation: Compliance with zoning laws requires the manager to make sure that the building is used in accordance with its classification. This may include the type of building use, its density, size, and proximity to other buildings.

questions.question: A property manager is assessing bids from potential ‘contractors’. Which of the following factors is MOST important when making a decision?
answers: That the contractor is a personal friend of the property manager and has a good social standing within the community.
That the contractor has offered the lowest price regardless of their experience, certifications or level of insurance.
That the contractor is fully licensed, insured, has all required certifications and a solid history of completing quality work.
That the contractor has the most modern vehicles, and the best company branding, regardless of any other qualifications.
feedbacks: A personal relationship is not a valid business metric.
Cost should not be the only driver of selection.
This is the most important factor when selecting a contractor.
This is not a metric for assessing the capabilities of a contractor.
questions.explanation: Qualifications, licensing, insurance, and a proven history of quality and reliability are key when selecting a new vendor.

questions.question: What is the definition of 'Net Operating Income' (NOI) in real estate?
answers: The gross rental revenue from a property before any deductions.
The gross potential rental income from a property, less any vacancy and credit losses.
The effective gross income from a property, minus all operating expenses.
The total revenue from a property, less all operating expenses, debt service, and capital expenditure.
feedbacks: This is gross income not NOI.
This is the Effective Gross Income not the NOI.
This is the correct definition of NOI.
This is the cash flow not the NOI.
questions.explanation: Net Operating Income is a calculation of the income of a building, with all operating costs removed. It does not include any debt service or financing costs.

questions.question: A property manager is developing a ‘tenant retention’ strategy. What should be the PRIMARY focus of this strategy?
answers: To ensure that there are no changes to the property and that everything remains as it is.
To only focus on attracting new tenants to the property and to ignore the needs of the existing tenants.
To actively communicate with tenants, address any issues, and create a welcoming and engaging community to ensure tenants feel valued.
To impose stricter rules and regulations on the tenants in order to minimize the number of complaints or requests they may have.
feedbacks: This will not improve tenant satisfaction or retention.
Ignoring existing tenants will not be beneficial to the property.
This is the main focus when creating a retention strategy.
This is counterproductive and will reduce tenant satisfaction.
questions.explanation: An effective retention strategy must be based around understanding the needs of the tenants and finding effective ways to improve their experience of living in the property.

questions.question: A property manager has a legal responsibility to protect 'tenant privacy'. Which of the following actions would be considered a breach of this responsibility?
answers: Entering a tenant’s apartment without providing the required legal notice.
Sharing a tenant’s payment history with a third party marketing company.
Regularly communicating with tenants by email.
Sharing any photos of a tenant, with another member of staff on the property.
Only discussing tenant issues with them directly, and not with any other tenants.
Publicly displaying tenant data, for example in the communal areas of the building.
feedbacks: This is a breach of privacy.
This is a breach of privacy.
This would not be considered a breach of privacy.
This is a breach of privacy.
This is good practice and would not be a breach.
This is a clear breach of privacy.
questions.explanation: Entering a property without proper notice, sharing data with third parties, releasing photos and publicly displaying personal data are all examples of data breaches and should not happen.

questions.question: A CPM is reviewing a lease for a commercial property.  The lease contains a 'percentage rent' clause.  What best describes this type of clause?
answers: Rent is based on a fixed amount plus a percentage of the landlord's operating expenses.
Rent is calculated based on a fixed base rent plus a percentage of the tenant's gross sales.
Rent is determined by a percentage of the appraised value of the property.
Rent is adjusted annually based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
feedbacks: This describes an expense stop or pass-through provision, not percentage rent.
This is the correct definition of a percentage rent clause.
Appraisal value is not typically used for percentage rent.
Rent escalations are different from percentage rent.
questions.explanation: Percentage rent is a common component of commercial leases where the landlord receives a base rent plus a percentage of the tenant's sales, aligning landlord's income with tenant's success.

questions.question: A property manager is developing a capital improvement budget for a large apartment complex. Which of the following would NOT typically be considered a capital improvement?
answers: Replacement of the HVAC system for the entire complex
Installation of new energy-efficient windows in all units
Repainting the hallways and common areas
Resurfacing the parking lot
feedbacks: This is a major upgrade with long-term benefit and is a capital improvement.
This is a long term improvement and should be categorized as a capital improvement.
Painting is a routine operating expense.
Resurfacing is an improvement of the property and would be a capital expense.
questions.explanation: Routine maintenance like painting is an operating expense, not a capital improvement. Capital improvements add to the value or extend the life of the property.

questions.question: Which of the following ethical principles requires a property manager to act in the best interest of their client, even if it means foregoing personal gain?
answers: Autonomy
Beneficence
Justice
Non-maleficence
feedbacks: Autonomy relates to self-governance and choices, not acting in the client's interest.
Beneficence implies acting for the good of others, which includes the client.
Justice refers to fairness, not explicitly prioritizing the client's interest over personal gain.
Non-maleficence means avoiding harm, not actively prioritizing a client's best interest.
questions.explanation: Beneficence is the core ethical principle that requires a professional to prioritize the well-being and interests of their client, even if it conflicts with their own desires or potential gains.

questions.question: A tenant has abandoned a leased commercial space, leaving behind significant personal property. The lease is silent on procedures for abandoned property. Which action should the property manager take FIRST, under common legal practice?
answers: Dispose of the property immediately to clear the space for re-letting.
Immediately rent the space to a new tenant and allow them to deal with the property.
Make a reasonable attempt to notify the tenant of the abandoned property, following legal guidelines.
Contact local law enforcement to remove the property immediately.
feedbacks: This is not advisable and could lead to legal claims from the tenant.
This can expose the landlord to potential issues with regards to the ownership of the abandoned items.
This is the required first step to ensure both the landlord and tenant's rights are protected.
Police action will not be required until legal steps have been taken.
questions.explanation: In cases of abandoned property, it is the primary legal obligation of the landlord to attempt to notify the tenant before any actions to dispose of the property. This is required to avoid potential legal actions.

questions.question: A property manager needs to calculate the Net Operating Income (NOI) for a commercial building. Which of these is the CORRECT formula?
answers: NOI = Gross Potential Revenue + Operating Expenses
NOI = Effective Gross Income - Operating Expenses
NOI = Gross Potential Revenue - Debt Service
NOI = Effective Gross Income + Capital Expenditures
feedbacks: This formula does not produce the correct NOI calculation.
This is the correct method to calculate Net Operating Income.
This is not the correct NOI calculation method.
Capital expenses are not deducted in the NOI calculation.
questions.explanation: The formula for Net Operating Income is calculated as Effective Gross Income less all Operating Expenses.

questions.question: When is the use of a security deposit to cover wear and tear permitted under standard lease agreements?
answers: The security deposit can be used for any repairs needed due to the tenant's negligence and normal wear and tear.
The security deposit cannot be used to cover normal wear and tear but can be used for tenant-caused damage.
The security deposit can be used for major repairs, regardless of the cause.
The security deposit can only be used for rent defaults and nothing else.
feedbacks: Security deposits are not typically used to cover wear and tear.
This is the correct protocol for security deposit use.
This would not be the correct use of the security deposit.
Security deposits can be used for more than rent defaults.
questions.explanation: Security deposits are generally used to cover tenant-caused damages beyond normal wear and tear, unpaid rent, or other breaches of the lease agreement.

questions.question: A property manager is evaluating several bids for a major roof replacement project. Which factor is LEAST likely to be a primary consideration in selecting a contractor?
answers: The contractor's previous experience with similar projects.
The lowest bid from a qualified and reputable contractor.
The contractor's current backlog and project schedule.
The contractor's personal relationship with the property manager.
feedbacks: Experience is a crucial factor for the successful completion of a project.
Cost is a consideration but not the only one.
The contractor's schedule is a practical consideration for timely completion of work.
A personal relationship should not factor into the decision making process.
questions.explanation: The contractor should be chosen solely on their professional experience, cost and capability. A personal relationship should not be a deciding factor, particularly in a bid process.

questions.question: A property manager is dealing with a tenant who has failed to pay rent for several months. The tenant is uncommunicative and refuses to vacate. What is the NEXT step the property manager must take?
answers: Change the locks and seize the tenant's possessions.
Continue sending late notices and threatening legal action.
Begin formal eviction proceedings through the court.
Negotiate a payment plan with the tenant directly
feedbacks: This is an illegal self-help eviction.
Continued notices without legal action does not move the situation forward.
This is the correct legal process for eviction.
Direct negotiation with an uncommunicative tenant is unlikely to achieve results.
questions.explanation: When a tenant is not paying and refuses to vacate, the property manager must begin a formal eviction procedure.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the function of a 'sinking fund' in property management?
answers: A fund to cover unexpected emergency repairs.
A fund specifically for annual tax payments on the property.
A fund that is set aside over time to pay for future large capital expenses or replacements.
A fund that is used to cover monthly operating expenses.
feedbacks: This fund is used for larger projects that have been planned.
This is not the correct use for a sinking fund.
This is the correct purpose of a sinking fund.
Operating expenses are part of the normal operational budget.
questions.explanation: Sinking funds are reserves set aside over time to fund large, non-recurring capital expenses, ensuring funds are available when needed without straining annual budgets.

questions.question: What does the term 'effective gross income' (EGI) in property management refer to?
answers: Total potential rental income of a property.
Total potential rental income minus operating expenses.
Total potential rental income minus vacancy and credit losses.
Total potential rental income minus debt service and capital improvements.
feedbacks: This is the Gross Potential Income.
This describes the Net Operating Income.
This is the correct definition of Effective Gross Income.
This is the Cash Flow of a property.
questions.explanation: Effective Gross Income is derived by subtracting an estimated vacancy and credit losses from the potential total rental income of a property.

questions.question: Which of the following is a critical responsibility of a property manager in maintaining an ethical standard of practice?
answers: Ensuring the property is marketed to the widest range of people, regardless of protected characteristics.
Prioritizing tenant needs over the landlord's financial goals.
Acting with transparency and disclosure in all financial transactions and property-related dealings.
Maintaining good relations with tenants to avoid legal disputes.
feedbacks: While important this does not define the key ethical requirement of the property manager.
The property manager is required to balance the needs of all parties.
This is the key ethical requirement for a property manager.
While this is important it does not focus on the ethical requirements.
questions.explanation: Transparency and full disclosure in all matters is a cornerstone of the ethical conduct of a property manager.

questions.question: A property manager is preparing a marketing strategy for a vacant commercial space. Which of the following should be their primary focus?
answers: Listing the property only on the least expensive websites.
Targeting a very niche demographic for the lowest price possible.
Highlighting unique features and benefits that align with the target tenant profile.
Overstating the positives about the property while downplaying any negatives.
feedbacks: Cost is a factor but should not be the primary one.
This is counterproductive and will restrict the amount of interest the property will receive.
This is the correct method of attracting the most suitable tenant.
This would be unethical and potentially illegal.
questions.explanation: Effective property marketing aims to attract the most qualified tenant using accurate information and showcasing the property’s best attributes.

questions.question: Which type of insurance policy will protect a landlord against a loss of rental income due to damage or vacancy after an insured event?
answers: General Liability Insurance
Flood Insurance
Renters Insurance
Business Interruption Insurance
feedbacks: This type of insurance is used to cover injury and property damage to a third party.
This type of insurance is for loss through a flood event.
This is a policy held by the tenant.
This is the best policy for loss of rental income.
questions.explanation: Business Interruption Insurance is used specifically to cover the loss of revenue in the event a business is interrupted by damage or other covered event.

questions.question: A property manager is investigating a tenant complaint of mold in their apartment unit. Which of the following actions should be taken FIRST?
answers: Immediately begin mold remediation efforts in the unit.
Dismiss the tenant's claim as likely exaggerated.
Conduct a thorough inspection to determine the extent of mold and its cause.
Offer the tenant to move to another unit.
feedbacks: Without a full inspection of the issue this is too quick to action.
This is not an acceptable response to the claim.
This is the correct first action to take.
Moving the tenant does not resolve the underlying mold issue.
questions.explanation: Before any action is taken on a claim, a full investigation needs to be done to determine the cause and the best remedial action.

questions.question: Which of the following actions would be considered a violation of Fair Housing Laws?
answers: Refusing to rent an apartment to a family with young children based on noise concerns.
Requiring a higher security deposit for tenants with pets.
Advertising an apartment as 'perfect for singles'
Rejecting an applicant based on a consistently poor credit score.
Limiting the number of guests allowed in a unit based on fire safety.
Implementing a 'no pets' policy for tenants.
feedbacks: This would be a clear violation of the Fair Housing Act.
Pet deposits are a permitted practice.
This can be discriminatory as it excludes families.
This is an acceptable reason to reject an applicant.
This is an acceptable safety precaution.
A 'no pets' policy can sometimes be a violation of the Fair Housing Act.
questions.explanation: Refusal to rent to families with children, advertising to a limited demographic and applying a blanket 'no pets' policy can all be examples of violations of the Fair Housing Act.

questions.question: In a lease agreement, what does the 'covenant of quiet enjoyment' imply?
answers: The tenant has the right to hold loud parties and make noise at any time.
The landlord guarantees that the property will be kept free from defects for the duration of the lease.
The tenant has the right to use the property without unreasonable disturbance or interference from the landlord.
The tenant is entitled to complete silence at all times in the leased property.
feedbacks: This is not a part of the quiet enjoyment clause.
This is a separate issue under the warranty of habitability.
This describes the 'covenant of quiet enjoyment' correctly.
This is an unreasonable expectation and not part of quiet enjoyment.
questions.explanation: The covenant of quiet enjoyment assures the tenant's right to use the leased property without substantial interference from the landlord.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a due diligence period during a property acquisition?
answers: To ensure the seller meets the terms of the purchase agreement.
To allow the buyer to conduct a thorough review of the property's condition, financial performance, and legal status.
To secure financing for the property purchase.
To finalize the lease agreements with existing tenants.
feedbacks: This would be one of the main aspects of due diligence but not the primary purpose.
This is the key purpose of a due diligence period.
This occurs outside of the due diligence period.
Lease agreements would be reviewed as part of the due diligence.
questions.explanation: Due diligence is done to ensure the buyer can make a full informed decision based on the facts relating to the property before purchase.

questions.question: Which document will MOST accurately detail the planned improvements, maintenance schedules, and repair guidelines for a property?
answers: Lease Agreement
Property Management Agreement
Property Maintenance Manual
Monthly Property Report
feedbacks: This document outlines the tenant and landlord obligations, not the maintenance plan.
This is an agreement between the property owner and the property management company.
This is the best document to detail the planned improvements, maintenance schedules, and repair guidelines.
This report is a summary of monthly activity and not a planned document.
questions.explanation: A property maintenance manual details the planned maintenance schedule and procedures for managing the property.

questions.question: A property manager is managing a multi-tenant commercial building. How would they calculate the CAM (Common Area Maintenance) charges to tenants?
answers: Based on the total rent each tenant pays.
Based on the percentage of rentable square footage each tenant occupies.
Based on the landlord's total operating expenses for the property.
Based on a predetermined flat fee agreed upon by all tenants.
feedbacks: CAM charges are not usually linked to rent.
This is the standard method for calculating CAM charges.
This is part of the calculation but not the way it is allocated to tenants.
A flat fee is not the typical method to assign CAM charges.
questions.explanation: CAM charges are usually allocated to tenants based on their percentage of rentable square footage within the building.

questions.question: In the context of environmental regulations, what does 'Phase I Environmental Site Assessment' entail?
answers: Sampling and laboratory analysis of soil and groundwater for contaminants.
A historical and visual inspection of the property for signs of potential contamination.
Implementing a remediation plan to clean up existing contamination.
Monitoring the property for ongoing environmental issues.
feedbacks: This is part of Phase II, not Phase I.
This is the correct description of a Phase I assessment.
This is the remediation phase.
This is an ongoing task and not part of Phase I.
questions.explanation: A Phase I assessment primarily involves historical records research, a site visit, and interviews to identify potential environmental liabilities.

questions.question: A property manager is considering installing a new security system in an apartment building. What should be the PRIMARY concern?
answers: The aesthetic appeal of the new security system.
The cost of the system alone.
The effectiveness of the system in deterring crime and improving tenant safety.
The potential for the system to create extra work for management.
feedbacks: Aesthetics are not the primary concern.
Cost is a factor, but not the primary.
This is the key consideration.
This is not a valid reason to ignore security needs.
questions.explanation: When it comes to security, the primary concern should always be the protection of tenants and property through an effective system.

questions.question: What is the role of a 'holdover' clause in a lease agreement?
answers: To describe the process of early lease termination.
To specify the terms for a tenant who continues to occupy the property after the lease expires.
To outline how disputes between landlord and tenant should be resolved.
To describe the process for subletting a property.
feedbacks: This is not a function of the holdover clause.
This is the purpose of the holdover clause.
Dispute resolution is not a holdover clause issue.
Subletting is a separate issue from the holdover clause.
questions.explanation: A holdover clause specifies what happens when a tenant continues to occupy the space after the lease expiration and typically defines the new rental rate and the terms of occupancy.

questions.question: Which action by a property manager would BEST demonstrate their fiduciary duty to a landlord?
answers: Accepting a cash payment from a tenant, without issuing a proper receipt.
Using a tenant's security deposit to cover personal expenses temporarily.
Negotiating the best possible lease terms and property management fees for the landlord.
Prioritizing personal interests over the landlord's needs.
feedbacks: This would be considered unprofessional and negligent.
This is a breach of trust and would be considered fraud.
This would best demonstrate their fiduciary responsibility.
This is a conflict of interest and unethical.
questions.explanation: The property manager has a fiduciary duty to act in the owner's best interest, this includes getting the best terms and fees.

questions.question: A property manager is overseeing a large renovation project. Which task would NOT be part of their standard role in project management?
answers: Developing and managing the project budget and timeline.
Negotiating with contractors and vendors for the best prices and services.
Physically carrying out the construction or renovation work themselves.
Ensuring the project is completed in compliance with all relevant codes and regulations.
feedbacks: This is a standard role of the manager.
This is a standard role of the manager.
This is not the role of the property manager.
This is a standard role of the manager.
questions.explanation: A property manager oversees the overall renovation process, but does not typically carry out any of the physical labor or construction themselves.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical component of a 'property management agreement'?
answers: The scope of services the property manager will provide.
The fees and compensation structure for the property manager.
Detailed personal information about the property manager’s family and private life.
Procedures for lease administration, rent collection, and tenant relations.
feedbacks: This would be a typical clause within the management agreement.
This would be a typical clause within the management agreement.
This is not typical nor required in the property management agreement.
This is a typical clause within the management agreement.
questions.explanation: Personal details about the property manager is not part of the property management agreement.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY concern when a property manager is dealing with an emergency situation, such as a fire in a building?
answers: To protect the building's structure and minimize damage.
To ensure the property manager's own personal safety and well being first.
To ensure the safety and well-being of the tenants and anyone on site.
To immediately evaluate the total financial loss and seek insurance payment.
feedbacks: Protecting life should be the primary concern.
Protecting life should be the primary concern.
This is the key and most important concern for the property manager.
Financial considerations are not the primary concern in an emergency.
questions.explanation: In an emergency situation, a property manager must act to ensure the immediate safety of all tenants and individuals on the property.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes a 'triple net lease' in commercial real estate?
answers: The landlord pays for all property expenses, including taxes, insurance, and maintenance.
The tenant pays only a set amount of base rent, and nothing else.
The tenant pays base rent plus a portion of the property taxes, insurance, and maintenance costs.
The tenant pays base rent plus all property taxes, insurance, and maintenance costs.
feedbacks: This is the opposite of a triple net lease.
This is a gross lease, not a triple net lease.
This describes a modified gross lease, not a triple net.
This is the correct definition of a triple net lease.
questions.explanation: In a triple net lease, the tenant pays base rent plus their share of property taxes, building insurance and maintenance costs.

questions.question: A property manager is considering implementing new policies for handling tenant disputes. Which approach is most effective for minimizing tenant conflicts?
answers: Adopting a strict, zero-tolerance policy with no exceptions.
Ignoring small complaints and only responding to major issues.
Establishing clear, consistent policies with a fair and transparent process for dispute resolution.
Relying on a case-by-case approach without any formal procedures.
feedbacks: This can lead to an increase in conflict.
This is not a sound management approach.
This is the best approach to handle disputes effectively.
This would make it difficult to enforce or manage.
questions.explanation: Clear, consistent policies and transparent procedures that are fairly applied in all cases can help to reduce disputes from occuring and help resolve them effectively.

questions.question: A property manager receives a formal complaint from a tenant about noise disturbances by another tenant. What should be their first step in addressing this issue?
answers: Contact the tenant who is creating the noise and impose fines immediately.
Immediately begin eviction proceedings against the noisy tenant.
Conduct an investigation to determine the validity of the complaint, and assess the level of disturbance.
Ignore the complaint as a minor issue that will resolve itself.
feedbacks: This would not be the first step.
This is not an appropriate first step.
This is the most appropriate first step.
Ignoring a tenant complaint is unprofessional and bad practice.
questions.explanation: A full investigation of the nature of the noise issue, including interviewing both parties, is the most sensible first step.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'Americans with Disabilities Act' (ADA) for property managers?
answers: It requires that all properties must provide unlimited free parking for handicapped tenants.
It sets the minimum acceptable standards of building maintenance on every property.
It requires that properties are accessible for people with disabilities and that no one is discriminated against based on their disability.
It limits the amount of service animals that can be present on a property.
feedbacks: This is not an element of the ADA act.
This is not an element of the ADA act.
This is the key principle of the ADA act.
The ADA act does not limit service animals, only pets.
questions.explanation: The ADA requires that properties are accessible to those with a disability, and no one is discriminated against based on their disability.

questions.question: A property manager is tasked with disposing of hazardous waste from a commercial property. What is the most critical factor in handling this situation?
answers: Ensuring the waste is disposed of quickly and cheaply.
Following local, state, and federal regulations regarding hazardous waste disposal.
Avoiding any environmental impact of the hazardous waste.
Documenting the process of disposal and keeping records for future use.
feedbacks: Cost should not be the driver of a hazardous waste disposal.
Compliance should always be the key issue when dealing with hazardous waste.
This is a component of compliant disposal.
This should be done but not the most critical factor.
questions.explanation: Compliance with local, state and federal guidelines, including how it is disposed, transported and stored, are all required when dealing with hazardous waste.

questions.question: What is the definition of 'capitalization rate' (cap rate) in real estate investment?
answers: The ratio of a property's purchase price to its gross potential income.
The rate of return on the equity invested in a property.
The ratio of a property's net operating income to its market value or purchase price.
The annual cost of debt service on a property.
feedbacks: This is not the correct description of a cap rate.
This is the Return on Investment not the cap rate.
This is the correct definition of capitalization rate.
This describes the debt service.
questions.explanation: Cap rate is the relationship between a property's net operating income and its market value, used for investment analysis.

questions.question: What does the term 'tenant improvement allowance' (TIA) typically refer to in a commercial lease?
answers: A payment for tenant damages to be used at the lease end.
A contribution from the landlord to the tenant to improve or customize the lease space.
A penalty paid by the tenant to the landlord for early lease termination.
A set fee paid by the tenant to the landlord for common area maintenance.
feedbacks: This is the opposite of TIA.
This is the typical use of TIA.
This is an early termination penalty, not TIA.
This is part of the CAM charges.
questions.explanation: A Tenant Improvement Allowance is provided by the landlord to the tenant to customize or improve the space to meet their specific needs.

questions.question: A property manager is faced with the decision to increase the rent on a property. What should be their primary consideration when setting the rent increase?
answers: Maximizing the property owner's profit regardless of market conditions.
Keeping the increase as high as possible, as long as tenants are willing to pay.
Ensuring the rental rate is competitive in the local market while maintaining an acceptable ROI for the property owner.
Following a simple across-the-board percentage increase without regard to unit condition or demand.
feedbacks: Rent should always be based on the current market.
This would be considered unethical and not best business practice.
This is the correct approach for rent increases.
A blanket approach is not effective.
questions.explanation: Rent increases should always be inline with local market rates whilst still meeting the owner's needs and ROI expectations.

questions.question: In a standard property management agreement, what is the primary purpose of an 'indemnification clause'?
answers: To define the property manager's responsibilities in maintaining the property.
To protect the property manager from liability for actions taken on behalf of the owner.
To outline the specific procedures for rent collection and late fees.
To specify the terms for contract renewal between the property manager and the owner.
feedbacks: This is not the function of the indemnification clause.
This is the purpose of the indemnification clause.
This is part of the general agreement and not an indemnification issue.
Contract renewal is separate from indemnification.
questions.explanation: The indemnification clause protects a manager from liability arising from their actions on behalf of the owner, so long as they are not negligent.

questions.question: A tenant is refusing to allow the property manager access to the property, despite proper notice for a necessary repair. What is the property manager’s legal right of action?
answers: Enter the property without notice as it is an emergency repair.
Contact the police and ask for assistance in entering the property.
Obtain a court order granting access to the property for the repair work.
Terminate the lease immediately for the tenant's breach of contract.
feedbacks: This may be considered a trespass and a violation of tenant rights.
This action is too strong without further legal advice and action.
This is the correct course of action after failed access attempts.
This is not the correct first action in this situation.
questions.explanation: When a tenant refuses access after proper notice, the manager will need a court order granting them access to the property.

questions.question: What is the significance of a 'Certificate of Occupancy' (CO) in property management?
answers: It is a document that proves the ownership of the property.
It is a document that outlines the lease conditions.
It is a document issued by a local government authority certifying that a building is suitable for occupancy.
It is a document required to secure property insurance.
feedbacks: This is a deed, not a CO.
This is the function of the lease agreement.
This is the purpose of the Certificate of Occupancy.
This document is not a Certificate of Occupancy.
questions.explanation: A Certificate of Occupancy is issued after building inspections, confirming that the property meets code and is suitable for occupancy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a generally accepted accounting principle (GAAP) that a property manager should follow?

questions.question: A property manager is preparing a 'pro forma' for a potential property acquisition. What information would they NOT include in this document?
answers: Projected rental income, vacancy rates, and operating expenses.
Debt service payments and potential financing options.
Detailed information about existing tenant disputes and personal tenant details.
Estimated property value and potential return on investment.
feedbacks: This would all be included in a pro forma.
This is also required in the pro forma document.
This would not be included in the pro forma document.
This would be included in the pro forma document.
questions.explanation: A pro forma only includes financial forecasts, not details of disputes or private information.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most important aspect of managing the finances of a property?
answers: Keeping the finances private and only accessible to the property manager.
Ensuring transparency, accuracy, and timely financial reporting to all stakeholders.
Minimizing expenses even if it results in property neglect.
Prioritizing personal financial gains over the financial interests of the owner.
feedbacks: This would be poor practice and highly irregular.
This is the key requirement in property finance.
This would cause issues for the long term.
This is unethical and illegal.
questions.explanation: Transparency, accuracy, and timely reporting is key when it comes to property finance, this ensures all parties are aware of the finances at all times.

questions.question: A property manager discovers that a tenant has sublet their unit without prior consent of the landlord. What is the most appropriate course of action?
answers: Ignore the situation, as long as the rent is paid in full each month.
Immediately evict both the tenant and the sub-tenant, as this is a breach of contract.
Review the lease for clauses relating to subletting, then issue a notice of breach of lease to the tenant.
Contact the tenant and verbally explain that subletting is not allowed, and then leave it at that.
feedbacks: Ignoring this situation is poor practice.
This is not the correct first action.
This is the correct approach in this situation.
Verbal communication is not sufficient when it comes to a breach of lease.
questions.explanation: Leases require prior permission for any subletting arrangements and failing this the correct procedure should be followed.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'gross potential income' (GPI) and 'effective gross income' (EGI) in property management?
answers: GPI is the actual rent collected, while EGI is the amount of rent that should be collected.
GPI is the actual rent collected, while EGI is the rent collected minus operating expenses.
