This is the key aim when creating a new system.
This is not the most effective and may be difficult to track.
This is not an effective method.
questions.explanation: A well structured system must be easily used by both tenants and staff, allowing all parties to track work through to completion.

questions.question: A property manager is responsible for 'asset management' of a property. Which of the following describes their role?
answers: Managing day-to-day property operations and tenants.
Focusing on short term goals and cash flow.
Creating and implementing strategies to maximize the value and performance of the asset.
Only focusing on tenant satisfaction and retention.
feedbacks: This is property management not asset management.
This is not the role of asset management.
This is the role of asset management.
This is part of property management not asset.
questions.explanation: Asset managers look at the long term investment goals, focusing on strategy for building value, maximizing performance, and enhancing overall asset worth.

questions.question: A property manager has received a formal complaint from a tenant about a breach of quiet enjoyment. What action should they take FIRST?
answers: Ignore the complaint as it is a minor issue that will likely resolve itself.
Immediately begin eviction proceedings against the tenant responsible for the noise.
Conduct a thorough investigation of the complaint, and assess the level of disturbance.
Contact the tenant and verbally dismiss the claim and ask them to deal with it themselves.
feedbacks: Ignoring the issue is bad practice.
This would be an inappropriate first action.
This is the most appropriate first step.
This is not an effective method of resolving the dispute.
questions.explanation: A full investigation is required when there has been a breach of quiet enjoyment. The manager will need to assess the validity of the claim and the level of disruption.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the term 'depreciation' in accounting for property management?
answers: The decrease in the market value of a property over time due to wear and tear.
The allocation of the cost of a property as an expense over its useful life.
The cost of regular maintenance and repairs for the property.
The total amount of debt owed on the property.
feedbacks: This would not be recorded as depreciation.
This is the correct definition of depreciation.
This would be considered operating expenses.
This is the debt liability of the property.
questions.explanation: Depreciation is the accounting practice of spreading the purchase price of a property over its estimated useful life, rather than expensing it all at once.

questions.question: A property manager is preparing to renew an existing lease for a commercial tenant. What should be their primary focus during this process?
answers: Keeping rent rates unchanged regardless of current market conditions.
Increasing rent rates as high as possible to maximize profits.
Reviewing the existing lease, assessing market rates, and negotiating new terms that work for both parties.
Forcing the tenant to renew a lease without offering any changes or alterations to the existing terms.
feedbacks: This is not best business practice and may mean a loss of earnings.
This would likely cause issues with the tenants and renewals.
This is the best method of lease renewals.
This may not be best business practice when it comes to lease renewals.
questions.explanation: Lease renewals are key for revenue generation and should always consider market conditions and offer a fair deal for both the landlord and tenant.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key part of a 'risk assessment' for a property?
answers: Identifying any potential hazards and their likelihood of occurring.
Ignoring any issues that may be too expensive to resolve.
Evaluating any preventative measures that can be taken.
Focusing only on risks that have occurred in the past.
Creating a report of all potential risks and solutions.
Using a blanket approach to all risks, regardless of the likelihood of them occurring.
feedbacks: This is a key part of the risk assessment process.
This would not be good practice.
This is part of the risk assessment process.
This is a limited view of risk and will not protect the property from future issues.
This is required after the risk assessment.
A risk assessment needs to look at the likelihood and impact of all potential risks.
questions.explanation: Risk assessment requires identification of potential hazards, creation of a preventative plan, and the creation of a report outlining risks, likelihood, and solutions.

questions.question: A property manager is responsible for providing a 'warranty of habitability'. What does this imply?
answers: The tenant is allowed to make any changes to the property, without permission from the landlord.
The property is guaranteed to be free of any maintenance issues at the start of any tenancy.
The property is safe, fit for human habitation, and is free of any material defects that could endanger the life, health or safety of a tenant.
The property manager is only responsible for the communal areas of the property, and not individual unit.
feedbacks: This would not be the warranty of habitability.
This is not what the warranty covers.
This is the meaning of warranty of habitability.
This is not the case, the manager is responsible for all areas of the property.
questions.explanation: The warranty of habitability states that a landlord is legally responsible to ensure a property is safe, habitable, and free from any issues that could affect life or health of the tenants.

questions.question: A property manager is assessing the 'capital improvement' needs of a property. What action would BEST exemplify this assessment?
answers: Scheduling routine maintenance tasks such as replacing filters in HVAC units.
Implementing a program to reduce tenant complaints.
Evaluating the need for major upgrades or renovations, such as new roofing, or appliance replacement.
Reviewing and updating the budget to account for tenant turnover.
feedbacks: This would be part of the maintenance schedule.
This is a management issue not capital improvements.
This is the correct use of a capital improvement assessment.
This is a standard budget management task.
questions.explanation: A capital improvements assessment looks at any upgrades or replacement to the major systems of the property.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of a 'property accountant' in property management?
answers: Managing day-to-day property maintenance and repairs.
Communicating with tenants about late payments.
Managing the financial records, preparing reports and ensuring accuracy in all transactions.
Setting rent rates and assessing market conditions.
feedbacks: This is not their area of responsibility.
This is a task for the property manager or a collections team.
This is the primary function of a property accountant.
This is a function of the property manager not the accountant.
questions.explanation: A property accountant is responsible for all financial records, budget creation, financial reporting, and ensuring that all funds are accounted for correctly and transparently.

questions.question: A property manager needs to improve the 'curb appeal' of a property. Which action would be the LEAST effective?
answers: Planting new flowers and landscaping the exterior.
Keeping the property clean and maintained including all communal areas.
Adding new exterior lighting to make it more attractive at night.
Ignoring any maintenance or repairs as long as the interior is well presented.
feedbacks: This can improve curb appeal.
This will increase curb appeal.
This is another method to improve the curb appeal.
This will decrease curb appeal.
questions.explanation: Ignoring maintenance and repair will degrade curb appeal and make it less appealing to a potential tenant.

questions.question: What is the primary role of a 'property leasing agent'?
answers: Managing day to day tenant issues and maintenance requests.
Managing and collecting tenant payments and late fees.
Marketing available units, screening prospective tenants, and finalizing leases.
Maintaining the overall physical condition of the property.
feedbacks: This would be a property managers role.
This is more in line with a property manager role.
This is the key role of a property leasing agent.
This is the responsibility of maintenance.
questions.explanation: A leasing agent's role is to market the property, screen potential tenants, and complete the leasing process from start to finish.

questions.question: A tenant makes a request for a specific repair which the property manager deems to be unnecessary and outside the terms of the lease. What is the correct course of action?
answers: Ignore the request to avoid unnecessary expenses.
Send a maintenance team immediately to carry out the requested work.
Review the lease, and provide a written explanation why the repair will not be carried out, citing specific lease terms.
Contact the tenant and discuss in person, refusing the request verbally.
feedbacks: This is not good practice and may cause legal issues.
This would be wasteful and not practical.
This is the best approach to the situation.
Verbal communication may not be sufficient, a written response is best practice.
questions.explanation: When a tenant requests a repair, the lease should be reviewed and then communicated with the tenant in writing.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST important factor when creating a 'budget' for a managed property?
answers: Maximizing the profit margin of the property, regardless of its practical implications.
Ensuring all costs are covered while aligning with the property’s goals and market conditions.
Using the budget to reward the property manager and any other staff with a large bonus.
Focusing solely on reducing expenses with little regard for the property's current or future needs.
feedbacks: The budget should be set to realistic figures, and market conditions.
This is the correct approach for budget creation.
A budget is for property needs, not personal rewards.
This would be an ineffective budget for long term management.
questions.explanation: A well planned budget will ensure all operating costs are covered, whilst also accounting for investment goals, and any potential risks.

questions.question: What is a main goal of 'preventative maintenance' programs?
answers: To deal with emergencies and fix issues as they occur, regardless of the cost.
To minimize the need for maintenance and repairs by ignoring minor issues.
To reduce the cost and frequency of major repairs by identifying issues in advance and carrying out regular scheduled maintenance.
To reduce staffing levels and decrease the cost of maintenance contracts.
feedbacks: This would be reactive maintenance not proactive.
Ignoring issues is not good business practice.
This is the main goal of preventive maintenance.
This will likely increase cost overall.
questions.explanation: Preventative maintenance aims to find problems early before they become major issues. This reduces downtime, repair costs, and overall operating costs.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common reason for a landlord to 'terminate a lease' early?
answers: Failure by the tenant to pay rent.
The tenant asking for reasonable accommodation for a disability.
The tenant making minor alterations to the property, with no permission.
The tenant complaining about the condition of the property.
The tenant having a consistent low score on credit checks.
The tenant conducting illegal activities on the property.
feedbacks: This is a common reason for lease termination.
This is not a reason to terminate a lease and is discriminatory.
This is a common cause for lease termination.
Complaints are not a reason to terminate a lease.
Credit checks are done before a tenancy not during it.
This is a valid reason for early lease termination.
questions.explanation: Non-payment of rent, damage to property and illegal activity are all common and acceptable reasons to seek early lease termination.

questions.question: A property manager is trying to increase the occupancy rate of a property with a high number of vacant units. Which strategy would be MOST effective?
answers: Increase the rent rates to make it more desirable for prospective tenants.
Ignore the vacancies in the hope that they will become filled in time.
Review current market rates, marketing the property more effectively, and making minor upgrades to increase its appeal.
Reduce maintenance to save costs and make the property more affordable for potential tenants.
feedbacks: This is counter intuitive when aiming to increase occupancy.
This is an ineffective approach.
This is the most effective approach in this situation.
Reducing maintenance will lower the quality of the property overall and make it less desirable.
questions.explanation: A strategy must look at the market and assess the needs of any potential tenants. Marketing must be on point to reach these, whilst also making minor upgrades to make a property more attractive.

questions.question: A property manager is required to perform a 'reserve study' for a property. What is the primary goal of this study?
answers: To determine whether the rent rates should be increased for the next year.
To assess the current market value of the property.
To assess the current state of the property and develop a plan to ensure sufficient funds are available for any future capital expenses.
To determine if a particular tenant should be given a discount on their monthly rent.
feedbacks: This is not the purpose of a reserve study.
This is an appraisal and not a reserve study.
This is the purpose of a reserve study.
This would be separate to any reserve study.
questions.explanation: A reserve study will look at the current state of a property, and plan for future upgrades, repairs, and replacements, ensuring the property is fully funded for all future capex.

questions.question: A property manager is reviewing their insurance policy. Which type of cover would protect them from any lawsuits arising from a tenant discrimination issue?
answers: Professional Liability Insurance.
Errors and Omissions (E&O) Insurance.
General Liability Insurance.
Workers compensation insurance.
feedbacks: This would not be for tenant discrimination.
This type of insurance would provide coverage for discrimination lawsuits.
This is for personal injury or property damage not discrimination.
This is for employee injuries not discrimination.
questions.explanation: Errors and Omissions insurance will protect a business from potential legal claims arising from mistakes, or discrimination in the course of business.

questions.question: A tenant is requesting to 'sublet' their unit. What action should a property manager take first?
answers: Immediately deny the request to ensure there are no issues with the sub-tenant.
Ignore the request and hope that it will go away.
Review the lease agreement to see if subletting is allowed, and communicate the options to the tenant.

questions.explanation: The lease agreement must be reviewed, any policy for subletting is contained within, and then any options must be communicated clearly to the tenant.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of 'preventing tenant turnover'?
answers: To implement a strategy of high rent increases to increase profit.
To reduce costs by ignoring any tenant requests.
To ensure consistent income and minimize the time and expense of marketing and re-letting units.
To focus primarily on attracting new tenants, with little regard for existing tenants.
feedbacks: This is likely to cause increased tenant turnover.
This will not help with retention.
This is the primary goal of tenant retention.
This is not an effective strategy.
questions.explanation: Keeping existing tenants is a key to consistent revenue. Finding new tenants takes time, is more costly, and may cause issues in the property.

questions.question: A property manager has a responsibility to act ethically. What does this mean?
answers: Prioritizing the property owner’s desires above all other considerations.
Acting with complete transparency, integrity, and fairness in all property related dealings.
Maximizing profits by any means necessary, regardless of the tenants or the property.
Disclosing as little information as possible to all parties to avoid conflict.
feedbacks: This is unethical if it does not follow the terms of the lease, or the law.
This is the true meaning of ethical behavior.
This would be considered unethical and possibly illegal.
Transparency and disclosure are key to ethical behavior.
questions.explanation: Ethics require a property manager to act honestly, fairly, with integrity and transparency in all dealings, and with all parties.

questions.question: A property manager is required to adhere to all 'local building codes and regulations'. What does this entail?
answers: Only focusing on the interior of the properties, as this is the responsibility of the tenants.
Ensuring the property meets all local building codes, and all regulations are enforced at all times.
Ignoring building codes if it reduces costs and increases profitability.
Only complying with the building codes if a tenant requests the repairs or maintenance.

This is dangerous, and illegal.
Compliance is not a request, but an obligation.
questions.explanation: Compliance means that all building codes and regulations are met and maintained at all times. This is to ensure the safety and health of the building and its tenants.

questions.question: A property manager is reviewing their marketing strategy. What is the PRIMARY purpose of a 'marketing analysis'?
answers: To assess the profitability of the property and adjust pricing accordingly.
To determine the effectiveness of marketing efforts, and to adjust them to meet the marketing goals.
To set rental rates that are competitive within the current market.
To assess the current condition of the property and plan maintenance tasks.

This is part of the market analysis process.
This is part of the property maintenance process.
questions.explanation: A marketing analysis assesses the effectiveness of the current marketing and allows a manager to review any areas for improvement.

answers: Immediately deny any request, to ensure the lease terms are not changed.

questions.question: A property manager is conducting a 'financial audit' of a property. What is the primary goal of this audit?

To review and verify the accuracy of all financial transactions and reports.
To assess the maintenance records for the past year and create new tasks.

feedbacks: This is not the goal of an audit.
This is the definition of a financial audit.
This is not part of a financial audit.
This is not a financial audit.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT typically a part of a property manager’s duties regarding 'risk management'?

questions.question: Which of the following would be a critical component of a 'disaster recovery plan' for a property?

questions.question: What does the term 'amortization' refer to in the context of property management accounting?

The method of calculating annual property taxes on an asset.
The process of gradually writing off the cost of an intangible asset over a certain period.

questions.explanation: Amortization is used to depreciate intangible assets over a set period.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key aspect of effective 'tenant communication'?
answers: Communicating regularly and clearly with all tenants.
Being proactive with updates and information, instead of waiting to be contacted by tenants.
Using multiple channels of communication to meet all needs.

feedbacks: This is a key aspect of tenant communication.
This is a great strategy for good communication.
This is an important strategy for tenant communication.

questions.question: A property manager is required to comply with Fair Housing Laws. What is the key aim of these laws?

To ensure all rental prices are the same in any particular area.
To favor certain tenant groups over others, to ensure the smooth operation of a property.

questions.explanation: The Fair Housing laws seek to ensure that all tenants are treated equally, regardless of race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, or disability.

questions.question: A property manager is developing a 'tenant satisfaction survey'. What is the most important aspect when creating this survey?
answers: Ensuring that the survey is biased towards positive feedback.

Ensuring that the survey is clear, concise, and designed to gather actionable feedback from tenants.

questions.question: What is the definition of a 'triple bottom line' (TBL) in property management?
answers: To focus solely on financial performance when making any business decision.
A framework that considers people, planet, and profit when making business decisions.
To reduce costs by any means, regardless of the environmental or social impacts.
To prioritize the short term financial goals over all long term goals.
feedbacks: This does not consider the other factors of the TBL.
This is the definition of the triple bottom line.
This is not TBL.
This is a short sighted approach and not TBL.
questions.explanation: The triple bottom line framework takes into account all aspects of business, environmental impact and social responsibility.

questions.question: A property manager is reviewing their vendor contracts for cleaning services. What should they prioritize when choosing a vendor?
answers: The cheapest option available, regardless of quality or service.
The company's previous experience, adherence to all relevant safety and environmental standards, and the quality of their work.
The friendliness and likeability of the company’s management team.

questions.explanation: Experience, quality of service, insurance, and environmental standards are the key factors when reviewing a vendor contract.

questions.question: A property manager has noticed an increase in tenant complaints about parking at the property. What should be their first step in addressing this issue?
answers: Ignore the complaints and hope that the problem will resolve itself.

This may escalate the issues.
This is the best first action to take.

questions.explanation: An assessment of any issue should take place before a solution can be found, this should include tenant feedback and consideration for the best possible solution.

questions.question: A property manager is tasked with implementing an 'emergency evacuation plan'. What should be their PRIMARY focus?
answers: Keeping the costs of evacuation as low as possible, regardless of risk.
To ensure the safe and efficient evacuation of all tenants and staff, in the event of an emergency.
To only evacuate tenants who are in immediate danger, and leave any other tenants to their own devices.
To focus solely on the building structure and minimizing any property damage.
feedbacks: Cost should never be prioritized over safety.
This is the most important part of the emergency evacuation plan.

questions.explanation: The safety and well being of all tenants and staff must be the priority in all circumstances, this should be the primary focus.

questions.question: Which of the following actions would be considered a violation of the 'Fair Housing Act'?

Advertising a rental unit as being 'suitable for families'.

feedbacks: This is not a violation of the FHA.

questions.explanation: Asking protected questions, refusing reasonable modifications or advertising that excludes certain groups, are all violations of the Fair Housing Act.

questions.question: What is the significance of a 'lease commencement date' when calculating rent due?
answers: The date the tenant views the property for the first time.
The date the lease document is signed by all parties.
The date on which the tenant takes possession and the lease agreement becomes effective.
The date that the tenant gives notice they wish to lease the property.

This is the correct definition of the lease commencement date.

questions.question: Which of the following would BEST describe the 'due diligence' process when considering the purchase of a commercial property?
answers: To carry out a surface level assessment of the property and its main issues, while ignoring any minor faults.
To carry out an inspection of the property, assessing its physical condition and financial status only.

questions.question: A property manager is tasked with preparing a 'pro forma' for an upcoming project. What information should be included in the pro forma?

A detailed list of all maintenance tasks required for the project.
Detailed financial projections including income, operating expenses and profitability.

questions.question: What does the term 'subordination' refer to in the context of a mortgage or lease agreement?

A document setting the boundaries of a piece of land.
A legal process for reviewing the terms of a tenancy agreement.

questions.explanation: Subordination is used when a new agreement becomes secondary to a pre-existing agreement, for example a lease that is subject to an existing mortgage on the property.

questions.question: Which of the following actions by a property manager could lead to a violation of 'tenant privacy'?

questions.question: A property manager is considering installing new security cameras on the property. What is the PRIMARY ethical consideration?

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 'property inspection checklist'?

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the primary responsibility of a 'building maintenance' team?

Ensuring all tenant leases are up to date and legally valid.

feedbacks: This is the role of the property manager not maintenance.
This is a lease administration responsibility.
This is the main responsibility of the maintenance team.
This is the role of leasing staff not maintenance.
questions.explanation: Maintenance teams are required to ensure the upkeep and safety of a building and its surroundings.

questions.question: A property manager has a legal responsibility to provide a safe environment for all tenants. What does this entail?
answers: Ensuring that the property is as cheap to run as possible, regardless of any safety concerns.
Ensuring that the property meets all required safety standards and any known hazards are addressed and resolved.
Only making the bare minimum of safety improvements required by law.
Ensuring all repairs are only completed if requested by a tenant.
feedbacks: This is unethical and unsafe.
This is the correct definition of providing a safe environment.
This is not the correct approach, safety should always be a priority.
Repairs must be completed irrespective of requests to maintain property safety.
questions.explanation: A safe environment requires a property to be maintained, repaired and be fully compliant with all safety regulations.

questions.question: A tenant has requested a change to a lease agreement. What should the property manager consider when reviewing the change?
answers: The property manager’s personal preference and feelings toward the tenant.
The long term financial implications of the proposed change, and the tenant’s previous conduct.
The potential impact on only the current tenants involved in the lease modification request.
The impact on the overall relationship with the owner and not the tenants.
feedbacks: This should not be a consideration in any business decision.
This is key when reviewing a lease change.
The review must look at all tenants and not just the one making the request.
The financial impact must be taken into account as well as all the other parties involved.
questions.explanation: Any changes to the terms of a lease agreement must be fully considered for its financial impact and for any potential future issues. The tenant history is also a key part of the review.

questions.question: What is the definition of 'Net Operating Income' (NOI) in commercial real estate finance?
answers: The total amount of revenue from rent, less only the debt service costs.
The total rental revenue, less all operational expenses, but before debt payments.
The total rental revenue less all expenses, including debt payments and capital expenditures.
The total rent charged and not what is actually collected.
feedbacks: This does not reflect all of the costs.
This is the correct definition of Net Operating Income.
This is the calculation for cash flow not NOI.
This is the gross potential income and not the net.
questions.explanation: NOI is the total rental income less operational costs, but before debt or other finance related costs.

questions.question: A property manager is responsible for the 'asset preservation' of a managed property. Which of the following is the best way to describe this role?
answers: Only focusing on day-to-day tasks to keep the property running.
To generate as much income as possible, by all means necessary, without any regard to long term maintenance or planning.
To ensure the property is maintained and upgraded in order to preserve its value and maximize its lifespan.
To ensure only minor repairs are completed to keep costs low.
feedbacks: Asset preservation is a long term approach not daily tasks.
This is unethical and not the correct approach.
This is the role of asset preservation.
This is not the objective of the asset preservation plan.
questions.explanation: Asset preservation focuses on the long term goals of a property, and ensures its value and lifespan are protected through appropriate planning, upgrades and ongoing maintenance.

questions.question: Which of the following factors is MOST important when assessing a 'vendor' for landscaping services?
answers: The personal connections of the vendor with the property manager.
The vendor’s previous experience, their license and qualifications, and their ability to carry out the work reliably.
The cost of the vendor contract and any additional expenses.
The aesthetic appeal of the vendor's equipment and company vehicles.
feedbacks: A personal relationship should not be a factor in vendor selection.
This is the most important consideration for any vendor selection.
Cost is important but not the most important factor.
This is not a key metric when selecting a vendor.
questions.explanation: Reliability, experience, quality, and possession of the correct licenses and insurances are all required from a good vendor.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a 'security deposit' that is paid by a tenant?
answers: To be used as a last month rent payment, at the end of a lease agreement.
To be used for any maintenance repairs, without any regard for the tenant.
To be used for any damages, rent defaults, or any lease breaches caused by the tenant during the tenancy.
To be used to make capital improvements on the property during the tenancy.
feedbacks: This is not the function of a security deposit.
This is not an acceptable use for a security deposit.
This is the main purpose of the security deposit.
This would be incorrect and illegal use of the deposit.
questions.explanation: A security deposit is held to ensure the tenant complies with the lease and covers any breaches, damage, or defaults of their agreement.

questions.question: A property manager has a legal responsibility to adhere to 'local zoning laws'. What does this responsibility entail?
answers: To ignore zoning regulations to allow for a more cost effective and profitable property.
To only be concerned with zoning regulations when a tenant makes a complaint.
To ensure that all activities and operations on a property comply with local zoning laws and regulations.
To only adhere to zoning laws if the owner agrees that they are reasonable.
feedbacks: This is an illegal and unethical action.
This is not an acceptable course of action.
This is the key requirement for zoning laws.
The laws must be adhered to irrespective of a personal view.
questions.explanation: Zoning laws govern how properties can be used and a property manager is responsible for ensuring their properties comply with these regulations.

questions.question: A property manager is reviewing their 'emergency communication plan'. What aspect is MOST crucial for this plan?
answers: To only use one method of communication in the event of an emergency to reduce confusion.
To ensure the plan allows for clear and timely communication with all tenants and staff.
To only communicate with a small subset of staff to reduce workload.
To only communicate through methods that the property manager is most comfortable with.
feedbacks: Using multiple communication methods is always best practice.
This is the main requirement for an effective emergency communication plan.
All staff must be included in any emergency procedure.
The comfort of the property manager is not a primary driver for the communication plan.
questions.explanation: Clear, timely and effective communication with all parties is the most important element of any emergency communication plan.

questions.question: A property manager is attempting to resolve a dispute between two tenants. What would be the most effective approach?
answers: Side with the tenant that pays the highest rental rate.
Side with the tenant that has been on the property for the longest time.
Be impartial, and seek to establish the facts while looking for an acceptable resolution for all parties.
Ignore all concerns and hope the issue will resolve itself.
feedbacks: This is not an effective method to resolve a dispute.
This does not resolve the issue.
This is the correct approach to resolving a dispute.
Ignoring disputes is not good practice and may cause escalation.
questions.explanation: Remaining impartial, gathering the facts and working toward a solution acceptable to all parties is key to any successful dispute resolution.

questions.question: What is the definition of 'Operating Expenses' in the context of property management?
answers: The total amount spent on capital improvements during a financial year.
The total amount of debt service payments made during a financial year.
All the expenses relating to the day to day operation of a property.
Any cost relating to repairs, maintenance or upgrades to a property.
feedbacks: This would be capex not opex.
This is a finance cost not an operating expense.
This is the definition of operating expenses.
This may include both operating expenses and capital expenditure.
questions.explanation: Operating expenses are all costs relating to the daily running of a property such as utilities, maintenance, insurance, and salaries.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key objective of a tenant 'retention program'?
answers: Ensuring there is clear and proactive communication with all tenants.
Providing a reliable maintenance and repair service.
Implementing an aggressive rent increase program at each renewal.
Creating a safe and welcoming community environment for all tenants.
feedbacks: This is a key part of any retention program.
This improves tenant satisfaction and therefore retention.
This will have a negative impact on retention.
This will ensure tenants are happy to remain as tenants.
questions.explanation: Aggressive rent increases can cause tenant dissatisfaction and a higher turnover, which would be detrimental to a tenant retention program.

questions.question: A property manager is required to do a 'lead paint disclosure'. What must be included in this disclosure?
answers: Only an oral explanation of the risks of lead paint.
Confirmation that the property has been fully tested for lead paint.
Disclosure of any known presence of lead based paint, along with any associated hazards.
Only a legal document stating that the property has no lead paint present.
feedbacks: Oral explanations are not sufficient.
Testing is not a legal requirement.
This is the key requirement for disclosure.
A disclaimer must be made when there is a potential for lead paint.
questions.explanation: A lead disclosure must explain all known instances of lead paint, any related hazards and be presented in writing to all tenants and buyers.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of a 'property manager' regarding property insurance?
answers: To only ensure there is a basic, affordable policy on the property, and not review any further.
To review insurance cover regularly, to ensure it is sufficient for the needs of the property, and is up to date.
To always opt for the lowest price policies regardless of any cover they offer.
To only review the insurance policy after an incident has occurred.
feedbacks: This is not an appropriate strategy for risk management.
This is the correct role of a property manager.
Price should not be the only driver.
This would not be an appropriate approach to risk management.
questions.explanation: A property manager must ensure the cover of their insurance policy is appropriate for the property and its circumstances, and reviews this on a regular basis.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of using a 'property management software system'?
answers: To only keep an accurate record of all tenant contact information.
To only track all rent payments and financial transactions.
To automate and streamline operations, and improve efficiency and communication.
To replace all maintenance staff with an automated system.
feedbacks: The system can do much more than this.
The system is capable of much more.
This is the intended purpose of the system.
This is not the function of a software system.
questions.explanation: Property software is used to improve efficiency, reduce errors, improve communications, and manage all aspects of a property and its tenants.

questions.question: What does the term 'quiet enjoyment' refer to in a lease agreement?
answers: The right of the tenant to hold parties and play loud music at any time of the day.
The tenant's right to make a reasonable level of noise, without causing disturbance to other tenants.
The tenant's right to occupy the property without unreasonable disturbance or interference from the landlord.
The tenant's right to demand complete silence at all times in the property.
feedbacks: This is not part of the quiet enjoyment clause.
This does not describe the covenant of quiet enjoyment.
This is the meaning of quiet enjoyment.
This is not a requirement of the covenant.
questions.explanation: Quiet enjoyment requires the landlord to ensure that a tenant can use and enjoy the property without constant interruption or disturbance from the landlord or other parties.

questions.question: A property manager is performing a 'market analysis' to set appropriate rental rates. What should be the MOST important factor in their analysis?
answers: The personal preferences of the property manager when it comes to setting rates.
The past rental rates of the property, without any consideration for the local market.
The current supply, demand, and rent rates of comparable properties in the area.
Setting rental rates significantly above market value to maximize profits.
feedbacks: This should not be a consideration when setting rates.
The local market must always be reviewed.
This is the most important aspect when setting rates.
This will likely reduce interest and lead to vacancies.
questions.explanation: A market analysis must look at the supply, demand, and rent rates of other comparable properties to ensure the new rental rates are competitive.

questions.question: Which of the following is a KEY responsibility of a property manager in the event of a tenant emergency?
answers: To always prioritize their own personal safety first above all other considerations.
To attempt to keep the costs of any resolution as low as possible, regardless of the emergency.
To ensure the immediate safety of the tenant, and to take all necessary steps to resolve the emergency, following all safety procedures.
To completely avoid all responsibility and leave the tenant to resolve the issue themselves.
feedbacks: While important, this should not be the priority in a tenant emergency.
This is not a factor in a tenant emergency.
This is the most important responsibility in any tenant emergency.
This is not an acceptable action in any emergency.
questions.explanation: The immediate safety of any tenant, in the event of any emergency, is a key responsibility of the property manager, and they must act immediately and effectively.

questions.question: A property manager is required to keep 'accurate financial records' for a property. What does this responsibility entail?
answers: Using a cash basis for all accounting to simplify the process.
Only keeping financial records for the past 6 months, to save space.
To ensure all financial transactions are properly recorded, with receipts for all expenditure, and all records are stored safely and securely.
To keep all property financial records as private as possible and only share them with the property owner when it is absolutely necessary.
feedbacks: Cash basis accounting is not a generally accepted practice.
Records must be kept for a longer period than six months.
This is the key responsibility when keeping financial records.
Transparency is important when it comes to finance.
questions.explanation: All financial transactions, must be recorded correctly, and transparently, whilst also providing all required records and documentation as and when they are required.

questions.question: A tenant has contacted the property manager, to report that there is a significant leak from a burst pipe in their unit. What should be the property manager's first action?
answers: To ignore the issue, as it is likely the responsibility of the tenant to resolve.
To contact all contractors for the cheapest quotes for the repair.
To turn off the water supply to the unit immediately, and then assess the damage.
To request that the tenant deals with all aspects of the repair and then submits the bill.
feedbacks: This is unacceptable and may cause more damage.
The main aim is to stop the water damage before commencing repairs.
This is the required first action.
This would not be an effective way to handle a leak.
questions.explanation: A water leak must be contained as quickly as possible to reduce the potential damage, turning off the water supply is the key first step.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT typically a component of a 'lease agreement'?
answers: The monthly rental rate and payment schedule.
Specific details of the property and all services and amenities.
The political views or religious beliefs of the tenant.
The terms and conditions for occupancy and any responsibilities of both the tenant and landlord.
feedbacks: This is a required element of a lease.
This is an element of the lease.
This would be illegal and inappropriate information for a lease.
This is required in a lease.
questions.explanation: Personal beliefs and religious views are not part of a lease agreement, and it is illegal to ask tenants about this information.

questions.question: What does the term 'capitalization rate' (cap rate) mean in commercial property management?
answers: The ratio of debt service to the value of the property.
The rate of return based on the property's equity.
The ratio of the net operating income to the current value of the property.
The amount of annual rent that is paid to the owner of the property.
feedbacks: This is the debt service ratio not the capitalization rate.
This is the return on equity not cap rate.
This is the meaning of cap rate.
This would be the gross rent and not the cap rate.
questions.explanation: Cap rate is used in investment analysis and is the result of dividing the Net Operating Income by the current market value of the property.

questions.question: A property manager is creating a new 'preventative maintenance' schedule for a property. What is the best strategy when doing this?
answers: To only schedule the bare minimum amount of maintenance to save costs.
To focus on a rigid set of tasks, without any regard for the condition of the property.
To prioritize regular inspections, routine tasks, and timely repairs to prevent any major issues.
To only schedule any maintenance when requested by a tenant.
feedbacks: This can lead to issues in the future.
The plan must be driven by the property's needs.
This is the correct approach to a preventative schedule.
This is reactive rather than preventative.
questions.explanation: A preventative maintenance schedule must include inspections, routine maintenance and timely repairs, with a focus on stopping issues before they become major problems.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key element of an effective 'tenant communication' system?
answers: Only relying on one single method of communication in all instances.
Using a clear and timely communication system that offers multiple channels for communication.
Only providing important information verbally and not in writing.
Only providing information if it is requested by the tenant.
feedbacks: This would be ineffective and may miss important messages.
This is the best approach to tenant communication.
This can lead to miscommunication.
Proactive communication is a better approach.
questions.explanation: A communication plan should be clear, timely and effective, with multiple channels available, and the ability to adapt to all circumstances.

questions.question: A property manager is seeking to maximize the 'energy efficiency' of a managed property. Which of the following actions would be most effective?
answers: Switching to low cost but inefficient and older model lighting fixtures.
Installing energy efficient appliances and fixtures such as low flow toilets.
Implementing a program of recycling and composting waste.
Ensuring all windows are double glazed and well sealed.
Ignoring building upgrades in an attempt to reduce costs.
Installing solar panels to produce clean energy.
feedbacks: This is counterproductive to efficiency.
This will improve building energy efficiency.
This is a good practice for environmental impact but does not improve energy efficiency.
This will improve thermal efficiency and reduce energy consumption.
Ignoring upgrades will lead to higher costs in the future.
This will improve energy generation and is a great option for energy efficiency.
questions.explanation: Installing efficient appliances, ensuring windows are sealed properly and generating power via renewable sources, are all examples of improving energy efficiency.

questions.question: A property manager needs to prepare an 'operating budget' for the upcoming year. Which of the following is essential to include in this document?
answers: A detailed plan for future property expansions and upgrades.
Detailed information about each tenant, and their individual payment history.
Detailed financial forecasts for all revenue, expenses, and any reserves required.
A detailed assessment of any potential market competition.
feedbacks: This is part of the capital budget not an operating budget.
This is not required in the operating budget.
This is the main requirement for the operating budget.
This is part of the market analysis and not an operating budget.
questions.explanation: The operating budget will require a forecast of all expected revenue, all operating expenses and details of any reserves that are required.

questions.question: What is the significance of an 'estoppel certificate' during a commercial property sale?
answers: To provide an accurate report of all capital improvements on the property.
To provide all historical details about the previous owners of the property.
To provide a certified record of the current lease terms and tenant obligations.
To record the value of the property as assessed by an independent professional.
feedbacks: This is not the role of the estoppel certificate.
This is not the intended function of the estoppel certificate.
This is the purpose of the certificate.
This would be a valuation report, not an estoppel certificate.
questions.explanation: The estoppel certificate verifies the key lease details for all tenants, and is used in the due diligence process during a property sale.

questions.question: A property manager has a legal responsibility to provide a 'warranty of habitability' to all tenants. Which of the following is part of this warranty?
answers: The tenant is not allowed to make any changes to the property during the tenancy.
The property must be in a state that makes it safe and healthy for human occupation.
The landlord is only responsible for the communal areas, and not the individual units.
The landlord is only responsible for any issues if they are reported by the tenant.
feedbacks: This is a lease clause not warranty of habitability.
This is what the warranty of habitability means.
This is not correct, the landlord is responsible for all areas of the property.
The landlord is responsible whether reported or not.
questions.explanation: The warranty of habitability means that a property must be safe and healthy for its occupants and free from any hazards that could cause harm.

questions.question: A property manager is responsible for 'tenant screening'. Which of the following is the primary goal of this process?
answers: To attract tenants that are able to pay the highest possible rental amounts.
To reduce the amount of applications by making the application process as difficult as possible.
To ensure that all tenants meet the required criteria, and have the ability to pay rent on time, whilst also meeting all other lease obligations.
To ensure all tenants are from a specific background, or have similar lifestyles.
feedbacks: This is not the primary goal of screening.
This is not an effective method of tenant screening.
This is the aim of the screening process.
This is discriminatory and illegal.
questions.explanation: Tenant screening is to ensure that any applicant has the ability to comply with all the lease terms and be a responsible tenant, whilst also complying with all relevant legislation.

questions.question: A property manager receives notice that a tenant is planning on leaving their lease early. Which is the MOST appropriate first action?
answers: To ignore the notice, as the tenant is legally obligated to the terms of the lease.
To immediately start eviction proceedings to remove the tenant from the property.
To review the lease and identify any clauses regarding early termination, and then communicate options to the tenant.
To change the locks immediately and hold the tenant to the full term of the lease.
feedbacks: Ignoring is not good practice.
Eviction is not an appropriate response.
This is the best first action.
This is illegal and ineffective.
questions.explanation: When a tenant is terminating a lease early, the best practice is to review the lease agreement and then communicate all options, and any penalties.

questions.question: What is the MOST important factor when evaluating potential 'contractors' for a maintenance project?
answers: To use the contractor that is known to the property manager.
To always choose the contractor that provides the lowest initial quote.
To select the contractor with the relevant experience and qualifications for the specific type of job.
To pick the contractor that is the most friendly and approachable.
feedbacks: A personal relationship should not drive a business decision.
The lowest cost is not necessarily the best contractor.
This is the key factor when selecting a contractor.
A personality match should not be a driver.
questions.explanation: Relevant experience, possession of correct licenses, insurances and qualifications are all necessary when selecting a contractor.

questions.question: A property manager is trying to improve the 'curb appeal' of a building. Which of the following is the LEAST effective method for achieving this goal?
answers: Planting new landscaping and flowers around the perimeter of the property.
Repairing any damage, and painting the exterior of the building.
Ignoring any maintenance, and focus on minor cosmetic changes only.
Installing new and up to date lighting fixtures in the exterior of the building.
feedbacks: This is an effective way to improve curb appeal.
This is a good method for improving curb appeal.
This will have a negative impact on curb appeal.
This will improve the curb appeal.
questions.explanation: Ignoring any maintenance requirements and focusing only on minor cosmetic changes, will not be effective in the long run and will actually degrade the overall curb appeal.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the primary goal of 'risk management' in property management?
answers: To only prioritize financial profits above all other factors.
To always avoid all potential risks, irrespective of the cost.
To identify and minimize potential risks to the property, tenants and the owner.
To always place blame on the tenants for all types of incidents that may occur.
feedbacks: Profitability is not the only driver of risk management.
This would be unrealistic and impractical.
This is the main purpose of risk management.
This is an unacceptable and ineffective approach to risk management.
questions.explanation: Risk management is a detailed process of identifying all potential risks, then assessing how these can be minimized to ensure safety and protection for the property and all associated parties.

questions.question: What is the definition of 'Cash Flow' in the context of real estate?
answers: The annual revenue of a property, before taking into account any expenses.
The effective gross income minus the total debt service payments.
The net operating income, minus all debt service payments.
The total amount of capital expenditures that were carried out on a property.
feedbacks: This is the gross income not the cash flow.
This is not the correct definition of cash flow.
This is the correct definition of cash flow.
This is separate from the cash flow calculation.
questions.explanation: Cash flow is calculated as the Net Operating Income less all costs associated with servicing any debt.
